posts.post_title: Can a Witness Be Forced To Testify for a Savannah Car Crash Case?
posts.post_content:
If you are seeking compensation for damages in a car crash case that goes to trial, you could greatly benefit from the testimony of a credible witness. However, if that witness does not want to go to court, can he or she be forced to testify? Below we discuss potential legal options if a witness refuses to go to court to provide testimony for a car crash case. Do you need legal help after being injured in a Savannah car crash? At Roden Law, we have been helping victims injured in collisions for decades. Our car crash attorneys in Savannah are prepared to help you recover the full and fair compensation you need.

Call our law offices 24/7 to discuss your situation. We are here to help you. 1-844-RESULTS

How Can a Witness Benefit the Outcome of My Case?

Credible witnesses can greatly benefit the outcome of a car crash case. Since they have no vested interest in the outcome of the claim, insurance companies, as well as the jury, give their statement more weight. Often witnesses may have had a different or clearer vantage point of the crash. He or she may have been better able to see events leading up to the point of impact. If the witness is not credible, his or her testimony could also negatively impact the outcome of your case. For instance, if he or she normally wears glasses and was not wearing them leading up to the crash. Witnesses with a history of not being honest would also not be considered credible. However, your attorney will thoroughly vet any potential parties before clearing them as a witness.

When Would I Need a Witness To Testify?

A witness may not be needed for every car crash case. However, there is no way of knowing that at the onset of a claim. This is why we strongly recommend gathering contact details of any witnesses at the scene of the incident. Your attorney can contact the witness soon after to vet them and determine if they are credible. Some of the reasons that you may need a statement or testimony from credible witnesses may include: In a car crash claim, a witness may be needed to provide a statement in several situations:
  • Determining Fault: When fault is not clear, a credible witness may be able to clarify who caused the accident.
  • Supporting Evidence: Statements from bystanders may back up your version of what happened.
  • Traffic Violations: In a "he said, she said" situation, testimony may answer a question about whether someone broke traffic rules.
  • Insurance Claims: Testimony can help when insurance companies want more information before agreeing to settle claims. It could also give your attorney more leverage to negotiate for a higher amount.
  • Legal Cases: In court, witnesses can help prove what happened.
  • Pedestrian Involvement: A bystander may have seen a pedestrian or cyclist may have contributed to the accident.
  • Visibility Issues: For example, when bad weather or blocked views are factors for the drivers and one or more witnesses had a better vantage point.
  • Complex Crashes: In accidents, such as a multi-vehicle crash, witness testimony can be invaluable.
  • Impact Details: Witnesses may often have more details that help to describe how serious the crash was.
  • Correcting Police Reports: When there are mistakes or missing details about the moments leading up to the crash in the police report.
Witness statements can be crucial to a case as they help paint a clearer picture of the crash.

What If Your Case Goes to Court and a Witness Refuses To Testify?

There are a few reasons why a witness may refuse to testify if your case goes to court. For starters, a lot of people hate the idea of having to testify in any trial. Even the idea of it is scary for some people. If a witness refuses for whatever reason, your attorney may be able to reassure that person enough to change his or her mind.

Serving a Subpoena if the Witnesses Refuses to Testify

Despite an attorney’s best efforts to convince a witness to testify voluntarily, he or she may still refuse to do it. In that situation, your attorney may consider serving the witness with a subpoena. Sometimes a witness may refuse to testify for valid reasons that may release them, even if you issue a subpoena, such as:
  • The court is more than 100 miles from the home or business of a witness
  • The witness claims an undue hardship makes it impossible for them to show up
  • A difficult witness may make it impossible for them to be served a subpoena
Most of the time, witnesses tend to be well-meaning and willing to help out. Even those who are less willing can often be talked into it by an experienced attorney.

We have decades of experience and a history of proven results. Our firm is dedicated to fighting for the full and fair compensation that you need after being injured in a car crash. posts.post_title: What Are My Legal Options After a Rideshare Crash in Charleston?
posts.post_content:
Rideshare services, like Uber and Lyft, offer a service of convenience, making it easy to get around Charleston. While most rides end without incident, do you know what legal options you have if you get into a crash involving a rideshare driver?

Table of Contents

  • Who Is Liable for a Rideshare Crash?
  • Who Pays for My Damages?
  • What Type of Compensation May I Seek from a Rideshare Crash?
  • How Long Do I Have to File a Legal Claim?
  • Were You Involved in a Rideshare Crash? Speak With a Roden Law Attorney
If you were hurt in a crash involving a rideshare driver, you may wonder what legal options you have for recovering compensation. At Roden Law, we understand your concerns, and we can help answer your questions. Call our Charleston car crash lawyers to discuss your situation — there is no cost for an initial consultation — and learn whether you may have a case.

Request your FREE consultation today at 1-844-RESULTS.

Who Is Liable for a Rideshare Crash?

There are many contributing factors that impact who may be liable in rideshare crashes. To start with, it is important to determine what happened, which is why investigators carefully examine the crash scene and talk to the drivers involved. They will also get statements from any witnesses who saw the crash as it happened. Getting video coverage may be more likely when a rideshare driver is involved. Lyft and Uber drivers sometimes install a dashcam in their vehicles as further protection in the event they are involved in a crash. Depending on the outcome of the investigation and the story the evidence tells, multiple parties could be responsible. Below are some parties who may be fully or partially liable for damages resulting from a rideshare crash:
  • Rideshare Drivers: Uber, Lyft or other rideshare drivers could be liable if their negligence led to the crash that injured you.
  • Other Drivers: Other drivers who hit the Uber or Lyft car you were riding in may be responsible, or at least partially liable for the crash.
  • Vehicle Manufacturer: The manufacturer of a defective rideshare vehicle could be liable if the defect contributed to the crash.
  • Government Entities: Though less common, a local or state agency may be liable if poor road conditions results in a crash, especially if it is due to a lack of maintenance.
  • Rideshare Companies: Uber, Lyft and other rideshare companies might share liability in certain circumstances.

Who Pays for My Damages?

Any compensation you may be eligible for will typically come from the insurance policy of the party or parties deemed liable. In rare cases, it could come from some where else, such as a government entity or another third party. In a rideshare crash, you may be eligible to seek compensation for your medical costs and other damages from the following sources:

Rideshare Company Insurance

Both Uber and Lyft provide insurance coverage for their drivers. The coverage available, however, depends on the driver's status at the time of the accident:
  • If the app was off, the driver's personal insurance applies.
  • If the app was on but no ride had been accepted, the company provides limited liability coverage.
  • If a ride was accepted or a passenger was in the car, the company provides up to $1 million in coverage.

At-Fault Driver's Insurance

If another driver caused the crash, their insurance would be the primary source of compensation.

Your Own Insurance

Your personal auto insurance, might sometimes come into play as well. This is particularly true if the at-fault parties have insufficient coverage or no coverage. In a situation like that, your uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage would help to cover your damages. For instance, say an at-fault driver has some coverage, but it only covers 70 percent of your compensation. If eligible, then you may be able to cover the remaining 30 percent of your damages through your uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage.

Other Liable Parties

If a vehicle manufacturer or government entity is found liable, their insurance or funds would provide compensation.

What Type of Compensation May I Seek from a Rideshare Crash?

Every rideshare crash involves different scenarios, potentially requiring various compensation. In a high impact collision, rideshare passengers may have severe injuries that cause them to need compensation for surgery and other related medical bills. You may be entitled to several types of compensation such as:
  • Medical expenses: This covers emergency treatment, hospital stays, surgeries, medications and future medical care
  • Lost wages: If your injuries cause you to miss work, you can seek compensation for lost income, including future earnings if you're unable to return to your job.
  • Pain and suffering: This non-economic damage compensates for physical pain and emotional distress caused by the accident.
  • Property damage: If your personal property was damaged in the crash, you can seek compensation for repairs or replacement.
  • Loss of enjoyment of life: Compensate for injuries that prevent you from enjoying hobbies or activities, you once did before the crash
  • Punitive damages: Use to punish the wrongdoers in cases of extreme negligence or intentional misconduct

How Long Do I Have to File a Legal Claim?

In Georgia, you have two years from the date of the car crash to file a claim. The legal term for this deadline is the statute of limitations. Two years may sound like a lot of time, but it is important to remember that your attorney needs time to build a solid case. Injured victims who file late in the game give their attorney little time to get optimum results. If you miss the deadline, you will likely be barred from recovering any damages.

We have extensive experience and have a strong history of proven results. Call today for free consultation. We can help you determine what your next steps may be after a rideshare crash. If you choose our firm to represent you, there are no upfront costs or fees to pay.

posts.post_title: Soft-Tissue Injuries in Charleston: Your Guide to Filing an Injury Claim

Soft tissue injuries are less visible than fractures but could be just as debilitating. These types of injuries can vary from sprains to torn ligaments and could make everyday tasks uncomfortable.

Call our office at 1-844-RESULTS

Examples of Soft-Tissue Injury Claims

Victims may include the damages resulting from a soft-tissue injury in several different scenarios. If you were involved in these accidents, you may have a personal injury case.

Car Accidents

Car crashes are notorious for causing soft-tissue injuries;  whiplash injuries are especially common in collisions because of the violent back and forth jolting that occurs at impact. For example, in a rear-end collision, your head and neck can snap back and forth rapidly. This motion can strain or tear the neck's muscles, tendons and ligaments. This type of injury is extremely painful and could greatly limit the range of motion in your neck, shoulder and back area.

Slip and Fall Accidents

Slip-and-fall accidents can happen in public places, such as restaurants or office buildings. Occupants can fall if there are wet floors and no signs to warn them. Falls due to hazardous conditions, like wet floors or uneven surfaces, can result in strains, sprains and other soft-tissue injuries.

Workplace Accidents

Soft-tissue injuries are also common in the workplace. Victims who suffer this type of injury on the job may file for workers’ compensation. For instance, a construction worker could suffer a soft tissue injuries from lifting heavy materials, which could cause strain on muscles and ligaments. These injuries can happen if proper lifting techniques are not used.

How Is Liability Determined?

If the accident occurred in the workplace, victims do not need to prove negligence. They only need to be able to show that the accident and resulting injury occurred while they were performing their job duties. In a potential personal injury case, however, victims need to prove the other party was negligent. An attorney can help them determine negligence by proving that the other party had a duty of care.  For example, in a car accident case, drivers have a duty to operate their vehicles safely. Determining liability also includes:
  • Breach of Duty: A negligent party breaches their duty through actions or inactions. For instance, if a restaurant worker fails to put up a wet floor warning sign, a breach has occurred.
  • Causation: Next, the breach of duty must link to the victim's injury. This means proving that the defendant’s actions caused the accident that resulted in the soft tissue injury.
  • Damages: It is the victim’s responsibility to prove that they suffered actual damages through evidence such as invoices to show medical costs and employment records to show lost wages.

What Type of Medical Evidence Are Needed When I File a Claim?

Soft tissue injuries are harder to prove as the damage is not visible. However, there is evidence that can help you prove your claim and recover compensation:
  • Doctor’s reports
  • Hospital records
  • Test results
  • Physical therapy notes
  • Specialist reports
  • Medical records
  • Diagnostic test (X-rays, ultrasounds and physical examination)
Keeping a pain journal is something else you can do to help document your injury from day one, including pain levels and how it affects your overall quality of life.

Common Claims for Soft-Tissue Injuries

Every personal injury claim could result in different types of compensation. If you have suffered a soft-tissue injury due to another party’s negligence, you may be eligible for these types of compensation.
  • Medical Expenses: Coverage for medical treatments, physical therapy, medications and any necessary surgeries.
  • Lost Wages: Compensation for lost income due to injuries or inability to work while recovering from the injury
  • Pain and Suffering: Compensation for the physical pain, emotional distress, and reduced quality of life caused by the injury.
  • Future medical expenses: If the injury results in long-term or permanent disability, you may be entitled to compensation for future medical costs and lost earning potential.
  • Loss of Enjoyment of Life: If injuries prevent victims from enjoying daily activities or hobbies they once enjoyed.
  • Punitive damages: In some cases, this compensation will be awarded to victims if the at-fault party behaves recklessly or maliciously to deter future misconduct.
  • Rehabilitation costs: Expenses for rehabilitation services to help victims recover.

Types of Soft Injuries

Soft tissue injuries are damage to muscles, tendons or ligaments. For example, if someone twists or rolls their ankle, it could cause them to tear a ligament.  Muscles may be damaged if victims sprain an ankle, wrist, knee or foot. Soft tissue injury may include:
  • Strains: occur when muscles or tendons are overstretched or torn
  • Contusions: known as bruises and happen when a direct impact causes damaged blood vessels
  • Tendinitis: causes inflammation or irritation of the tendon, which connects muscles to bones
  • Bursitis: affects small, fluid-filled sacs called bursae located around significant joints like your shoulder, elbow, hip or knee

Treatment and Management

Soft-tissue injuries can result in significant pain, swelling, bruising, and a decreased range of motion. Effectively managing these injuries is crucial for proper recovery. Victims with minor soft tissue injuries may be able to recover with rest, ice, bandages, and keeping the damaged area elevated such as their leg or arm. However, severe injuries may cause victims to need surgery or prescribed medications.

While you focus on recovering an attorney can negotiate with the insurance company and determine your best interest. Roden Law is here to guide and support you throughout the legal process. We have a proven track record of securing compensation for our clients. Contact our firm for a free consultation. We can discuss your potential case and answer your legal questions. posts.post_title: How Delayed Injuries Could Impact Your Charleston Car Crash Claim
posts.post_content:
Some car accident victims do not realize that not all injuries manifest immediately after a collision. Delayed injuries can significantly impact your health and your ability to seek compensation.

Table of Contents

  • What are Delayed Injuries After a Car Crash?
  • How Delayed Injuries Affect Your Car Crash Claim
  • Proving Delayed Injuries for Your Claim
  • What Are the Long-Term Health Effects of Delayed Injuries?
  • Call Roden Law After a Charleston Car Accident
Below, our Charleston car accident lawyers discusses what delayed injuries could happen after a car crash and how delayed injuries can affect your claim. Also, we address how proving delayed injuries can help strengthen your claim. If you have been injured in a car crash, seek medical attention right away and legal counsel from a trusted attorney. At Roden Law, we are here to help you understand the next steps to take in the legal process.

Request your FREE case review today: 1-844-RESULTS.

What Are Delayed Injuries After a Car Crash

Delayed injuries are medical conditions that do not present symptoms immediately after a car accident. These injuries can emerge hours, days or even weeks after a collision. The human body's complex response to trauma along with adrenaline and shock, can mask pain and other injury symptoms. Common delayed injuries include:
  • Traumatic brain injuries that develop gradually
  • Soft tissue damage in muscles and ligaments
  • Whiplash-related to neck and spine complications
  • Internal bleeding or organ damage
  • Psychological trauma like post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)
  • Concussions and delayed neurological symptoms
  • Herniated discs that worsen over time
The absence of immediate pain does not mean you are uninjured. Professional medical diagnostic tests are crucial to rule out any serious medical conditions. Even if you feel fine initially, it is a good idea to seek medical attention immediately.

How Delayed Injuries Affect Your Car Crash Claim

Delayed injuries can significantly complicate the legal process of seeking compensation. Insurance companies often scrutinize claims where injuries are not immediately reported or documented. This makes understanding and properly addressing delayed injuries critical to protecting your legal rights. Key factors you should know about delayed injuries and filing claims include:
  • Medical documentation becomes paramount in proving your injuries
  • Waiting too long to seek medical treatment can weaken your claim
  • Insurance adjusters may argue that your injuries are unrelated to the accident
  • South Carolina's statute of limitations requires timely filing with complete medical evidence.
  • Financial compensation depends on detailed medical evidence

Proving Delayed Injuries for Your Claim

Successfully documenting delayed injuries requires taking the appropriate steps. It is important to file your claim with a licensed attorney that have experience with car accident cases because they can help you throughout the legal process. Some of the ways that you can strengthen your case if you have delayed injuries may involve:
  • Requesting Medical Records: If you go to the doctor and find out that you have injuries, get a copy of your medical records. Documents created close to the accident date serve as crucial evidence.
  • Documenting Medical Bills and Treatment: Keep a paper trail of your doctor appointments, prescriptions and any treatment related to your accident injuries. Preserve all medical bills, diagnostic reports and physician notes.
  • Follow Complete Treatment Plans: Adhere strictly to your healthcare provider's recommended treatment plan. Gaps in treatment can be used by insurance companies to challenge the severity of your injuries.
  • Keep a Personal Injury Journal: Record daily pain levels, medical treatments, emotional impacts and how injuries affect your work and personal life. Detailed documentation provides powerful narrative evidence.
  • Consult Medical Specialists: Some injuries require additional insight from neurologists, orthopedic surgeons,  and other medical professionals. These individuals can provide detailed assessments of the extent and severity of your injuries.

What Are the Long-Term Health Effects of Delayed Injuries?

Delayed injuries can have lasting impact beyond immediate medical concerns. Many victims underestimate the potential long-term health and financial consequences of seemingly minor post-accident symptoms. Some car crash victims may ignore injuries, assuming they will resolve with the treatment they are already receiving from their doctor. However, this assumption can result in delayed injuries going untreated. If you notice any new symptoms while being treated for existing car crash injuries, be sure to inform your doctor. They may need to create a new treatment plan or adjust your current one. Chronic pain, neurological complications and psychological trauma can develop months or even years after a car crash. These conditions may require extensive medical treatment, rehabilitation, and ongoing care, significantly disrupting your personal and professional life. Additionally, some delayed injuries can lead to permanent disability, affecting your future earning capacity and overall quality of life. Proactively documenting medical interactions, tracking symptom progression and working with medical professionals can help you receive appropriate care and support for a full recovery.

Do not let delayed injuries, compromise your legal rights or financial recovery. Our attorneys work tirelessly to ensure you receive full compensation for medical expenses, lost wages, pain and suffering and other damages. Time is critical in car accident claims. South Carolina's statute of limitations sets strict deadlines for filing personal injury lawsuits. Delaying medical treatment or legal action could permanently forfeit your right to compensation. Contact Roden Law today for a free consultation. There are no upfront costs or fees for our services.  We will review your case, explain your legal options and help you take the first steps toward seeking compensation.

posts.post_title: Can I Seek Compensation for Facial Injuries After a Charleston Car Crash?
posts.post_content:
When a victim sustains visible injuries to the face in a car crash, it can leave more than a physical injury. Visible scarring and disfigurement on a person's face can cause psychological harm, embarrassment and depression. It can also have a significant financial impact on both the victims and their families.

Table of Contents

  • What Kinds of Facial Injuries Happen in Car Crashes?
  • Common Causes of Facial Scarring and Disfigurement
  • How Much Compensation for Face Injury?
  • What Factors Impact My Compensation?
  • Call Roden Law After Facial Scarring or Disfigured in a Car Accident
If you have facial injuries that are significantly impacting your quality of life, we encourage you to speak to one of our Charleston car accident attorneys about your situation and potential legal options. Although compensation cannot change what has happened to you, it can help you get the medical care you need so you can continue to move forward with your recovery.

Schedule a free, no-risk consultation today: 1-844-RESULTS.

What Kinds of Facial Injuries Happen in Car Crashes?

A car accident can cause serious damage to facial bones, muscles, nerves and soft tissues. Below are some of the most common types of facial injuries caused by car crashes.

Soft Tissue Injuries

Cuts, bruises and burns across the face can result from broken glass or flying debris during a car accident. These injuries may range from minor scrapes to deep lacerations requiring plastic surgery. Even seemingly minor cuts on the face can leave permanent scars, affecting a victim's appearance and emotional well-being.

Facial Fractures

The face contains 14 different bones that can break during trauma. Common fractures include orbital fractures, which affect the eye socket, and cheekbone fractures, which are more likely to happen in side-impact collisions. Other types of fractures may include:
  • Nasal bone breaks from direct impacts
  • Cheekbone (zygomatic) fractures from side impacts
  • Jaw (mandible) fractures that affect eating and speaking
  • Upper jaw (maxilla) fractures requiring surgical repair

Dental Trauma

Dental trauma in a car accident typically happens when your head or mouth strikes an object or when the mouth abruptly closes due to the impact. For example, in a rear-end car accident, someone’s head or mouth can strike the steering wheel. Dental injuries during a car accident could be:
  • Broken or chipped teeth
  • Knocked-out teeth requiring immediate care
  • Fractured dental roots
  • Damaged gums and soft tissue
  • Jaw alignment problems affecting the victim's bite

Eye Injuries Trauma

Eye injuries from a car crash could leave victims with blurry vision or vision loss. Eye injuries may occur if the victim is struck in the face with a direct impact, such as from airbag deployment or shattered glass. Serious eye injuries may include:
  • Corneal scratches or tears
  • Orbital bone damage
  • Vision problems
  • Detached retina
  • Loss of eyesight

Nerve Damage

Facial injuries often involve some degree of nerve damage. The impact of a trauma may stretch, compress or even sever nerves. In a car accident, facial nerve damage happens when the impact forces the head or face against hard surfaces. Nerve damage may cause car crash victims to experience:
  • Loss of facial movement
  • Numbness or tingling
  • Problems with facial expressions
  • Difficulty eating or speaking
  • Chronic pain

Common Causes of Facial Scarring and Disfigurement

During a car crash, multiple factors can lead to facial scarring and disfigurement. The impact of a collision can be severe enough to thrust a victim's body and face against hard surfaces in the vehicle. Facial scarring and disfigurement may occur in a car crash as a result of:

Flying Glass and Debris

Shattered windshields and windows send sharp glass fragments flying through the vehicle at high speeds. These fragments can slice deep into facial tissue, causing severe lacerations that often result in permanent scarring. Side-impact collisions particularly increase the risk of glass-related facial injuries when windows explode inward.

Airbag Deployment Impact

While airbags save lives, their explosive deployment can cause serious facial injuries. The intense force and heat from deploying airbags can burn the skin, cause chemical burns or create facial abrasions. High-speed deployment may also drive debris into facial tissue.

Dashboard and Steering Wheel Impact

Sudden deceleration can throw drivers and passengers forward onto hard surfaces, like the dashboard or steering wheel. The resulting impact can break or crush facial bones and create wounds that cause permanent disfigurement.

Ejection Injuries

When victims get thrown from vehicles, their faces may hit window glass, metal from the vehicle or scrape across pavement. Road rash from sliding across asphalt can remove layers of facial skin. Additionally, impact with objects during ejection can shatter facial bones and create deep tissue damage.

Secondary Collision Damage

After the initial impact, loose objects inside the car become dangerous projectiles. Cell phones, water bottles and other items could strike the face. These secondary impacts often cause significant tissue damage and scarring.

Metal and Frame Intrusion

Sharp metal edges can penetrate the passenger compartment when a vehicle's frame collapses during impact. These twisted metal pieces can slice or puncture facial tissue, creating jagged wounds that are difficult to repair without visible scarring.

Burns and Chemical Exposure

Vehicle fires or chemical spills during crashes can cause severe facial burns. Thermal burns destroy tissue layers, while chemical burns from deployed airbags or leaking fluids can create permanent skin damage and discoloration.

How Much Compensation for Face Injury?

The amount of compensation you may receive for facial injury may vary depending on the factors and circumstances of your accident. However, insurance companies or courts may value your case depending on the expenses and damages you may incur.
  • Medical Expenses: Emergency room treatment, surgery costs, dental work, future medical needs, etc.
  • Lost Income and Earning Capacity: Facial injuries could mean you miss work, so you may receive compensation for loss of future earnings and loss of income due to recovery time.
  • Pain and Suffering: This compensation can cover physical pain from injuries, emotional trauma, depression and anxiety.

What Factors Impact My Compensation?

Different factors can impact your compensation. Some reasons why some cases may be valued at different costs may include:

Injury Severity and Permanence

The more severe and permanent your facial injuries, the higher your potential compensation. Insurance companies and courts will examine numerous elements such as depth and visibility of scarring, number of facial bones broken and extent of soft tissue damage.

Medical Documentation

Your medical documentation will serve as viable evidence for your legal case. Detailed emergency room records, surgery reports and photos can strengthen your case. Your attorney can also consult with medical experts to provide further clarity and testimony about the severity and extent of your injuries.

Liability and Fault

After a car crash, you must prove that the other party was at fault. It could affect your compensation if you are found to be partially at fault in a South Carolina car accident. For example, if you are 30 percent at fault and your compensation is $100,000, it will be reduced to $70,000.

Professional Impact

Facial injuries resulting from car accidents can significantly impact an individual's career. For example, if a car crash victim has a job that requires frequent public appearances or being in front of a camera, such injuries could affect their livelihood. This situation may lead to compensation covering reduced earning capacity or necessitate career changes due to disfigurement.

Quality of Life Changes

Courts and insurance companies may consider how facial injuries affect your daily life. If you experience life changes such as social anxiety, loss of enjoyment in activities or changes in personal relationships, be sure to provide evidence of these impacts. Some evidence you may use includes daily journals and records of canceled events or missed gatherings.

We are here to help you get the full compensation you deserve after a car crash. We do not charge any upfront costs to engage the services of our law firm. We only get paid if you do.

posts.post_title: Who May Be Liable for a Dangerous Underride Truck Crash in Charleston
posts.post_content:
Life changes forever when a passenger vehicle slides beneath a commercial truck in Charleston. These underride truck crashes are one of the most devastating accidents on South Carolina highways.

Table of Contents

  • What Is an Underride Truck Crash?
  • Why Underride Truck Crashes Are So Dangerous to Other Drivers?
  • Can I Seek Compensation for My Damages After an Underride Truck Crash?
  • Who May Be Liable for the Underride Truck Crash That Injured Me?
  • Common Causes of Underride Accidents in Charleston
  • Proving Who Is At Fault for Your Charleston Underride Truck Accident
  • Defensive Driving Tips to Avoid Underride Truck Accidents
  • Call Roden Law for Legal Help After a Charleston Truck Accident
If you have been involved in a commercial truck accident, seek legal assistance from a trusted truck accident lawyer. A qualified lawyer can help you understand your rights and answer any questions that you may have. At Roden Law, our Charleston truck accident attorneys have helped several underride crash victims identify all liable parties, from negligent truck drivers to manufacturing companies with dangerous vehicle designs. Do not face the aftermath of these complex crashes alone.

Schedule your free consultation today: 1-844-RESULTS

What Is an Underride Truck Crash?

An underride truck crash occurs when a smaller vehicle collides with a large commercial truck and slides underneath the truck's body or trailer. These devastating accidents happen when a passenger vehicle, like your car, SUV, or motorcycle, travels partially or entirely under the high clearance of a tractor-trailer. The height difference between commercial trucks and passenger vehicles creates a dangerous scenario. The upper part of the smaller vehicle can be crushed or cut off as it slides beneath the trailer.

Why Underride Truck Crashes Are So Dangerous to Other Drivers?

Underride truck crashes stand as some of the most lethal accidents on Charleston roads for several critical reasons.When your car slides under a truck, it hits your car's safety features. The truck strikes through the vehicle’s compartment or interior space, often hitting passengers' heads or necks. The tremendous weight difference compounds the danger. A fully loaded commercial truck can weigh up to 80,000 pounds, while your passenger vehicle typically weighs under 4,000 pounds. This extreme difference means even "low-speed" underride collisions can cause catastrophic damage. The aftermath of underride crashes can become just as dangerous as the crash itself. In other types of crashes, emergency responders may be able to get to victims easily. However, in underride crashes, emergency responders face extreme challenges. The complex entanglement of vehicles makes extraction difficult and dangerous, often delaying critical medical care when minutes matter most.

Can I Seek Compensation for My Damages After an Underride Truck Crash?

Yes, you can seek compensation after an underride truck crash in Charleston. These catastrophic accidents often leave victims with various expenses related to the crash, while still managing their current financial duties. South Carolina law allows injury victims to pursue compensation from all parties responsible for an underride accident. The compensation available often covers:
  • Pain and suffering
  • Property damage
  • Rehabilitation costs
  • In-home care expenses
  • Current and future medical expenses
  • Lost wages and diminished earning capacity

Who May Be Liable for the Underride Truck Crash That Injured Me?

After an underride truck crash in Charleston, identifying all responsible parties is necessary for securing the full compensation you deserve. Multiple factors and parties can contribute to these devastating collisions.
  • Truck Driver: May be liable if negligent driving contributed to the crash, such as sudden braking, improper lane changes, or failing to use hazard lights when stopped.
  • Trucking Company: May bear responsibility for inadequate maintenance of underride guards, improper training of drivers, or setting unrealistic schedules that encourage unsafe driving.
  • Truck Manufacturer: Could be liable if the truck was designed without adequate underride protection systems despite foreseeable risks.
  • Trailer Manufacturer: Often responsible for the design and installation of underride guards; may be liable if guards were inadequately designed or manufactured.
  • Maintenance Providers: Third-party companies responsible for truck maintenance may be liable if they fail to properly inspect or repair underride protection systems.
  • Parts Manufacturers: Companies that specifically produce underride guards may be liable if their products were defectively designed or manufactured.
  • Cargo Loading Companies: In some cases, improper loading can affect a truck's handling or braking ability, contributing to crash conditions.
  • Government Entities: May share liability if poor road design or maintenance contributed to conditions that led to the underride crash.
Each case requires a thorough investigation to determine which parties bear responsibility for the specific circumstances of the crash.

Common Causes of Underride Accidents in Charleston

Underride truck crashes in Charleston result from multiple safety failures that could have been prevented. These devastating collisions may occur when numerous risk factors are present, from inadequate safety equipment to poor visibility conditions. These are some of the reasons why an underride accident could happen:
  • Insufficient or damaged rear underride guards on trailers
  • Absence of side underride protection on commercial vehicles
  • Poor visibility of trailers at night or in low-light conditions
  • Inadequate reflective markings on trucks
  • Sudden stops by commercial vehicles without warning
  • Height mismatch between passenger vehicles and commercial trucks
  • Design limitations of current underride guard regulations
  • Failure to maintain a proper following distance behind trucks
  • Weather conditions affecting visibility (fog, rain, snow)
  • Trailer designs that extend beyond the protection of guards

Proving Who Is At Fault for Your Charleston Underride Truck Accident

An attorney’s help can sufficiently establish liability in an underride truck accident. If you have a valid case, it will require a thorough investigation and compelling evidence. The evidence collection process begins at the accident scene, where our investigators document critical details like trailer guard conditions, truck positioning, and road factors. Police reports provide official documentation of violations and preliminary fault assessments. Other forms of evidence are:
  • Truck driver logbooks reveal potential hours-of-service violations or falsified records that may have contributed to driver fatigue or inattention.
  • Electronic Control Module (ECM) data, the truck's "black box”, provides irrefutable evidence of the truck's speed, braking patterns, and driver actions in the critical moments before impact.
  • Witness testimony can provide forgotten information that both parties may not know about, especially from those who observed the truck driver's behavior before the collision.
  • Industry specific witnesses can help establish exactly how the underride occurred and document the connection between the crash mechanics and your specific injuries.
  • Maintenance records frequently reveal negligence in guard repair, lighting systems, or brake maintenance

Defensive Driving Tips to Avoid Underride Truck Accidents

Drivers who drive defensively can help prevent dangerous underride truck accidents. When you recognize the potential for an accident with these vehicles, it can lower your chances of a catastrophic crash.
  • Maintain Safe Following Distance: Always keep at least a four-second gap between your vehicle and any commercial truck. This buffer zone provides vital reaction time if the truck stops suddenly.
  • Stay Visible in Truck Mirrors: If you cannot see the truck driver in their side mirrors, they cannot see you. Position your vehicle where the truck driver can easily spot you.
  • Exercise Caution When Passing: Plan truck passing maneuvers carefully and execute them efficiently. Signal early, maintain a consistent speed, and do not return to the truck's lane until you can see the entire truck in your rearview mirror.
  • Anticipate Wide Turns: Commercial trucks require extra space for turns. When you see a truck signaling for a turn, never attempt to squeeze between the truck and the curb. This puts you directly in a side underride danger zone.
  • Increase Following Distance at Night: Reduced visibility makes nighttime driving particularly hazardous around trucks. Double your normal following distance after dark and watch for poorly marked trailers or non-functioning lights.
  • Be Weather-Aware: Frequent rainstorms, heavy fog, or tropical weather can reduce visibility. Reduce speed around trucks during adverse weather conditions.

Call Roden Law for Legal Help After a Charleston Truck Accident

The traumatic scene of an underride truck accident can lead to physical and emotional injuries. You do not have to face these devastating losses on your own. At Roden Law, we can help you navigate the legal process. Our experienced legal team will review your situation, explain your options, and fight tirelessly to secure the maximum compensation you deserve. We can determine if you have a valid case during a free consultation. We do not charge any upfront costs for our legal services.

posts.post_title: A Pedestrian's Guide to Claiming Lost Wages in Charleston
posts.post_content:
King Street is the vibrant heart of Charleston, but its mix of heavy foot traffic and vehicles creates real risks for pedestrians. When an accident occurs, the path to financial stability can feel as overwhelming as the incident itself.

Immediate Financial Steps After a Pedestrian Accident

The moments following a pedestrian accident on King Street in Charleston are often a blur of confusion and pain. While your health is the absolute priority, the actions you take in the first 24 to 48 hours can significantly impact your ability to secure financial compensation. It’s about creating a clear, undeniable record of events from the very beginning.

Here are the foundational steps to protect your financial future:

  1. Seek Immediate Medical Attention. Even if you feel fine, some injuries have delayed symptoms. A medical report from a doctor or an emergency room visit creates an official link between the accident and your physical condition. This is not just for your health, it is the cornerstone of your claim.
  2. Understand What "Lost Wages" Means. This term refers to any income you lose because your injuries prevent you from working. It includes your salary, hourly pay, and any other regular compensation you would have earned.
  3. Report the Accident to the Charleston Police. A police report is an objective, third-party account of the incident. It documents the time, location, parties involved, and any initial findings of fault. Insist on a report, as it provides crucial evidence.
  4. Start a Personal Journal. Write down everything you remember about the accident. In the following days, document your pain levels, medical appointments, and any days you miss from work. This journal becomes a powerful tool for demonstrating the accident's daily impact on your life.

These initial actions are not just procedural, they are the building blocks of a strong and successful claim for the financial disruption you have suffered.

Documenting Your Lost Income for a Claim

Once you have addressed your immediate health needs, the focus shifts to gathering the proof needed for your claim. This is where you move from reacting to the accident to methodically building your case. The goal is to create a clear financial picture that leaves no room for dispute. How you approach this depends entirely on how you earn a living.

Essential Documents for Salaried and Hourly Employees

For those with traditional employment, the paper trail is usually straightforward. Your employer’s records are your best ally. You will need to collect recent pay stubs to show your rate of pay and hours worked, along with W-2 forms to establish your annual earning history. A formal letter from your HR department or direct supervisor confirming the dates you were unable to work due to your injuries is also essential. This letter solidifies the connection between the accident and your absence from work.

Proof of Income for Self-Employed Individuals and Gig Workers

If you are self-employed, a freelancer, or a gig worker, the burden of proof rests more heavily on you. You must demonstrate your income history and the financial dip caused by the accident. This involves gathering 1099 forms, client invoices, and contracts. Profit and loss statements showing a clear drop in revenue after the accident are particularly persuasive. It is also wise to maintain organized professional records, from financial statements to a polished career profile, which helps solidify your employment status. The complexity of gathering these documents can be daunting, and our firm can help streamline this process to ensure nothing is missed.

Documentation Checklist for Lost Wages
Document Type W-2 Employees Self-Employed/1099 Contractors
Proof of Pay Rate Recent Pay Stubs Client Invoices or Contracts
Annual Earnings History W-2 Forms & Past Tax Returns 1099-MISC/NEC Forms & Past Tax Returns
Verification of Missed Work Formal Letter from Employer Profit & Loss Statements Showing a Dip
Business-Related Losses N/A Business Bank Statements & Canceled Contracts

Remember, "wages" can include more than just your base salary. Be sure to account for:

  • Missed overtime opportunities
  • Lost commissions or bonuses
  • Depleted sick leave or paid time off (PTO)
  • Lost contributions to a retirement plan

Defining the Full Scope of Your Compensation

Recovering from a pedestrian accident involves more than just the income lost while you were healing. The true financial impact can extend for months or even years, and a successful claim must account for this entire scope. This is where we look beyond the immediate and calculate the full, long-term consequences of your injuries.

It is important to understand the difference between lost wages and lost earning capacity. Lost wages cover the income you missed during your recovery period. Lost earning capacity, on the other hand, addresses a permanent or long-term reduction in your ability to earn money in the future. If your injuries prevent you from returning to your previous job or require you to take a lower-paying position, you are entitled to compensation for that future financial loss.

Beyond tangible financial losses, the South Carolina accident claim process allows you to seek compensation for pain and suffering. This acknowledges the physical discomfort, emotional distress, and diminished quality of life caused by the accident. That journal you started in the first few days is invaluable here, as it provides a detailed record of your daily struggles. In South Carolina, the at-fault driver's insurance is typically responsible for these damages, making clear proof of their negligence essential. Calculating these complex damages requires experience, and a skilled Charleston personal injury lawyer from our team can accurately assess the full value of your claim.

Managing Communications with Insurance Adjusters

Soon after your accident, you will likely receive a call from the at-fault party's insurance adjuster. It is critical to remember their role. The adjuster is not your advocate, their primary responsibility is to protect their company's financial interests by minimizing the payout on your claim. They are trained negotiators, and anything you say can be used to reduce your settlement.

Navigating these conversations requires caution and a clear strategy. Here are some critical rules to follow:

  • DO NOT provide a recorded statement. Adjusters often request a recorded call to "get your side of the story." These recordings can be analyzed and your words taken out of context to challenge your claim later. Politely decline and state that you will provide information in writing.
  • DO NOT speculate or guess. If you are unsure about a detail, it is better to say "I don't know" than to guess. Incorrect information, even if unintentional, can damage your credibility. Stick only to the facts you are certain of.
  • DO NOT accept an early settlement offer. Insurance companies may offer a quick payout before the full extent of your injuries and financial losses are known. These initial offers are almost always far less than what you are entitled to.

All communication should be factual, brief, and to the point. We strongly advise you to contact us for guidance before engaging in these critical conversations. Having a legal representative handle all communications with the insurer ensures your rights are protected from the start.

Why Legal Support is Key to Your Financial Recovery

Trying to manage a personal injury claim while recovering from an accident is an immense burden. This is where a dedicated legal advocate becomes your most important asset. A Charleston personal injury lawyer does more than just file paperwork, they level the playing field against powerful insurance companies and fight to secure the compensation you deserve.

Our role is to build a comprehensive case on your behalf. We analyze the police report, gather witness statements, consult with medical experts to understand your long-term prognosis, and meticulously calculate your total damages. This includes not only your current lost wages but also your future earning capacity and pain and suffering. We then handle all negotiations, shielding you from the pressure tactics of insurance adjusters.

We believe that everyone deserves access to justice, which is why we work on a contingency fee basis. This means you pay no upfront costs. Our fee is a percentage of the settlement we win for you, so if we do not recover money for you, you owe us nothing. This model ensures our goals are perfectly aligned with yours.

Most importantly, time is a critical factor. In South Carolina, you generally have three years from the date of the accident to file a lawsuit. As confirmed by legal resources like MDSW Legal, once this deadline passes, you lose your right to seek compensation forever. Acting promptly is essential. Legal support is the most effective way to recover lost wages in Charleston, SC, and ensure a fair outcome. Since many pedestrian incidents involve vehicles, our expertise also extends to complex car accident claims.

posts.post_title: Filing a Claim After a Hazmat Truck Crash in Charleston
posts.post_content:
The Unique Dangers of Hazardous Material Spills on Local Highways

Charleston County consistently ranks among the top counties in South Carolina for truck accidents, making a collision on congested routes like I-26 a constant threat. While any truck crash is serious, one involving hazardous materials introduces dangers that extend far beyond the initial impact. These materials are defined by their properties: they can be flammable, corrosive, toxic, or explosive. When a tanker truck overturns, the risk is not just twisted metal but also chemical burns from a spill, lung damage from invisible fumes, or the potential for a catastrophic explosion.

The true danger of a hazmat truck accident Charleston residents might face lies in its unseen consequences. Symptoms from chemical exposure, such as respiratory distress or neurological issues, may not appear for hours or even days after the incident. This delay can cause victims to underestimate the severity of their injuries. The Zebra reports that South Carolina has one of the highest rates of traffic fatalities per 100 million vehicle miles traveled in the nation, a statistic that underscores the existing risks on our highways. When hazardous cargo is added to the equation, those risks multiply, creating a situation where the air you breathe can become the most immediate threat.

Federal and State Rules for Transporting Hazardous Goods

Both the federal Department of Transportation (DOT) and South Carolina truck accident laws establish a high standard of care for any company transporting hazardous materials. These are not suggestions; they are legally mandated requirements designed to prevent disaster. When these rules are broken, it often points directly to negligence.

This complex regulatory system includes several key components:

  • Specialized Driver Credentials: A driver hauling hazardous materials cannot have just any commercial license. They must earn a commercial driver's license (CDL) with a specific hazmat (H) endorsement, which requires passing additional written tests and undergoing a thorough federal background check.
  • Vehicle Placarding: You have likely seen the diamond-shaped placards on the sides of tanker trucks. These are not decorative. They are a universal communication system designed to instantly inform first responders and the public about the exact type of danger the cargo presents, whether it is a flammable liquid or a corrosive substance.
  • Cargo and Route Regulations: Strict rules govern how hazardous cargo must be secured to prevent spills. Additionally, trucking companies may face restrictions on which routes they can take or the times they can travel through densely populated areas like Charleston.

A violation of any of these regulations, from an improperly licensed driver to a missing placard, can become powerful evidence. It establishes a clear link between a company’s failure to follow the law and the harm caused in a crash.

Immediate Steps to Take After a Hazmat Truck Accident

In the chaotic moments following a crash with a hazmat truck, your actions can protect your health and your legal rights. The situation is fundamentally different from a standard car accident, and safety must be your absolute priority. The risk of fire, explosion, or exposure to toxic fumes is real and immediate.

Follow these steps to protect yourself:

  1. Prioritize Safety Above All Else: Your first move should be to get away from the truck. Note the direction of the wind and move upwind to avoid inhaling potentially toxic fumes. A distance of at least 500 feet is recommended if possible.
  2. Call 911 Immediately: When you speak to the dispatcher, it is critical to state that the accident involves a truck with hazardous material placards. This information ensures that specialized hazmat response teams are dispatched along with police and paramedics.
  3. Seek Immediate Medical Evaluation: This is non-negotiable, even if you feel fine. As mentioned, symptoms from chemical exposure can be delayed. A medical evaluation creates a crucial, time-stamped record of your condition right after the accident, which is vital for any future claim.
  4. Gather Information (Only If Safe): If you are a safe distance away and not injured, try to document the scene. Use your phone to take pictures of the truck’s placards, its DOT numbers, the driver's name, the trucking company name, and their insurance information. Do not speak to the driver or company representatives about fault.

Once you are safe and have received medical care, understanding the complexities of a commercial vehicle collision is the next step. The regulations and liabilities involved in these cases are distinct from typical car accidents, which is why consulting with experienced Charleston truck accident lawyers can be crucial.

Post-Accident Safety and Information Checklist
Action Why It's Critical What to Do or Say
Move to a Safe Distance (Upwind) Avoids exposure to toxic fumes, fire, or explosions. Note the wind direction and move at least 500 feet away.
Call 911 Ensures specialized hazmat teams are dispatched. 'I've been in an accident with a truck that has a hazardous material placard.'
Seek Medical Attention Documents injuries and detects delayed symptoms from exposure. Tell the doctor you were in an accident involving a chemical spill.
Document the Scene (If Safe) Preserves evidence for your claim. Photograph placards, truck numbers, vehicle damage, and the surrounding area.

Documenting Evidence to Build a Strong Claim

After the immediate crisis has passed, the focus shifts to methodically building a case for hazardous material spill compensation. The foundation of any successful claim is thorough documentation. Insurance companies and corporate legal teams will scrutinize every detail, so your ability to present a clear, undeniable record of events and damages is essential. Successfully navigating a complex claim requires a systematic approach to gathering and organizing information, ensuring every detail supports your case.

Your evidence file should include:

  • The Official Police Report: This is the first official record of the accident. It contains the responding officer’s observations, witness statements, and initial determination of fault. You can request a copy from the Charleston County Sheriff's Office or the specific police department that responded to the scene.
  • Photographic and Video Evidence: Go beyond just your vehicle. If possible, capture extensive photos and videos of all vehicle damage, skid marks on the road, traffic signs, weather conditions, and any visible spills or container damage on the truck. This visual evidence helps reconstruct the accident scene.
  • All Medical Records: This is one of the most critical components. Keep every bill, prescription receipt, doctor’s note, diagnosis, and treatment plan. These documents directly link the accident to your physical injuries and the financial cost of your recovery.
  • A Personal Injury Journal: Start a daily log immediately. Each day, write down your physical pain levels, your emotional state, and any daily activities you can no longer perform, from working to simple household chores. This journal provides a powerful narrative of how the accident has impacted your quality of life.

Identifying All Potentially Liable Parties

In a commercial truck accident, liability is rarely simple. It often extends far beyond the person who was behind the wheel. Identifying every potentially responsible party is a critical step because it opens up multiple avenues for compensation, which is especially important in catastrophic hazmat cases where damages can be severe and long-lasting.

A thorough investigation may reveal that fault lies with several entities, including:

  • The truck driver for their direct actions.
  • The trucking company for negligent hiring, inadequate training, or forcing drivers to violate safety rules.
  • The owner of the truck or trailer if poor maintenance contributed to the crash.
  • The company that manufactured the hazardous material.
  • The team that loaded the cargo if it was improperly secured.

Untangling the web of corporate relationships, insurance policies, and contracts to pinpoint fault requires professional analysis. This process is a core part of any successful personal injury lawyer's strategy to maximize a client's recovery. A skilled Charleston truck accident attorney will investigate each of these possibilities to ensure all responsible parties are held accountable.

Understanding Compensation and South Carolina's Time Limits

If you were harmed in a hazmat truck crash, you have the right to seek compensation for your losses. These damages are typically broken down into two categories to ensure all your hardships are accounted for.

The first is economic damages, which cover tangible, calculable losses. This includes all current and future medical bills, lost wages from time off work, diminished future earning capacity if you cannot return to your job, and property damage to your vehicle.

The second is non-economic damages. These are intangible but equally real losses, such as physical pain and suffering, emotional distress, and the loss of enjoyment of life caused by your injuries. An I-26 truck accident claim involving chemical exposure, for example, can cause significant long-term anxiety and suffering.

However, there is a critical deadline. In South Carolina, you generally have only three years from the date of the accident to file claim for truck accident SC. If you miss this statute of limitations, you will almost certainly lose your right to compensation forever. Do not wait. Investigating these complex cases takes time, and evidence can disappear. If you have questions about your rights or how to proceed with a claim, do not hesitate to contact us for a consultation.

posts.post_title: How Poor Truck Maintenance Causes Charleston Accidents
posts.post_content:
The Hidden Dangers on Charleston's Roads

Commercial trucks are a constant presence on Charleston's main arteries like I-26 and US-17, and they pose a far greater public-safety risk than drivers realize. We see them as a source of traffic, but their presence is a far more significant public safety issue for Lowcountry residents. When a collision occurs, the immediate assumption is often driver error, like speeding or distraction. However, a more invisible threat is frequently the root cause: negligent vehicle maintenance.

A mechanical failure on an 80,000-pound vehicle is not a minor incident. It leads to devastating crashes, severe injuries, and complex legal fights that can overwhelm victims and their families. Understanding who is responsible when a truck is improperly maintained is not just a legal question. For those affected, it is an essential step toward securing justice and rebuilding their lives after a preventable tragedy.

Common Mechanical Failures Behind Truck Crashes

While driver error gets most of the attention, the mechanical condition of a commercial truck is just as critical. These are not simple passenger cars; their systems are complex, and when they fail, the results are catastrophic. Many of these failures are entirely preventable with proper upkeep.

Here are some of the most common maintenance-related issues that lead to wrecks:

  • Brake Failure: The air brake systems on semi-trucks are powerful but require meticulous maintenance. Unlike the hydraulic brakes in your car, they can fail due to issues like worn-out brake pads, compressed air leaks, or improper adjustments. When this happens, the truck’s stopping distance increases dramatically, often leading to a violent brake failure truck accident with little warning.
  • Tire Blowouts: Commercial truck tires endure incredible stress from heavy loads and high mileage. Under-inflation, worn treads, or defects can cause a sudden, explosive blowout. The driver can instantly lose control of the vehicle, causing it to swerve, jackknife, or roll over into adjacent lanes of traffic.
  • Critical System Failures: Beyond brakes and tires, other key components can fail due to neglect. Faulty steering mechanisms can make the truck impossible to control, broken suspension parts can lead to instability, and defective lights or signals can make the truck invisible at night.

Federal regulations mandate strict inspection and maintenance schedules specifically to prevent these problems. The aftermath of such failures often requires a specialized legal team, and the services offered by our Charleston truck accident lawyers focus on holding negligent parties accountable.

Assigning Responsibility for a Maintenance-Related Wreck

When a truck accident is caused by a mechanical issue, determining who is at fault is not always straightforward. Responsibility often extends beyond the driver to the company that owns the vehicle and sometimes even to third parties. Federal law establishes a clear chain of command for vehicle safety.

The Trucking Company’s Legal Duty

Under a legal principle known as vicarious liability, trucking companies are responsible for the actions of their employees and the condition of their equipment. The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) requires companies to systematically inspect, repair, and maintain their fleets. Failure to do so is a clear example of trucking company negligence. This duty is non-negotiable; a company cannot shift the blame to a driver if it failed to provide a safe vehicle.

The Driver’s Inspection Responsibilities

While the company holds primary responsibility for maintenance schedules, the driver is the first line of defense. Drivers are legally required to conduct pre-trip and post-trip inspections to check for obvious defects in the brakes, tires, lights, and other systems. If a driver notes a problem but operates the truck anyway, they may also be held partially liable.

Third-Party Liability

In some cases, the fault may lie with an outside party. A third-party maintenance shop that performed a faulty repair or a manufacturer that produced a defective part could also be held responsible for a resulting crash.

These duties are not suggestions. As highlighted by the FMCSA, they are detailed in federal regulations like those governing Parts and Accessories Necessary for Safe Operation.

Area of ResponsibilityTrucking Company's DutyDriver's Duty
Systematic MaintenanceDevelop and execute a formal maintenance and repair schedule for every vehicle.Not directly responsible for scheduling, but must operate within the system.
Pre-Trip InspectionsEnsure drivers are trained and required to perform inspections.Physically inspect brakes, tires, lights, and other key systems before every trip.
Reporting DefectsEstablish a clear system for drivers to report issues and ensure timely repairs.Report any discovered defect or malfunction in writing immediately.
Record KeepingMaintain detailed 'truck maintenance records' for at least one year.Complete and sign daily vehicle inspection reports (DVIRs).

Investigating Maintenance Records to Prove Negligence

Proving that a crash was caused by poor maintenance requires more than just pointing to a blown tire or failed brakes. It requires a deep investigation into the vehicle’s history. The most critical evidence in these cases is the truck maintenance records. These documents are the official paper trail of a truck’s life, detailing every service appointment, repair, and part replacement.

An experienced attorney scrutinizes these logs for red flags that point directly to negligence. Common indicators include:

  • Long gaps between service dates, suggesting the truck was not maintained according to federal or manufacturer guidelines.
  • Recurring mechanical problems that were repeatedly patched with temporary fixes instead of being properly repaired.
  • Missing or incomplete driver inspection reports (DVIRs), which can indicate that either the driver was not performing inspections or the company was not retaining the records as required.

When these records are cross-referenced with the driver’s Hours of Service (HOS) logs, a disturbing picture can emerge. It might reveal that a company pressured a driver to continue operating an unsafe vehicle to meet a tight deadline. Obtaining these crucial documents requires a formal legal request during the discovery phase of a lawsuit. This critical step is managed by a skilled attorney, and a Charleston personal injury lawyer from our firm can handle this complex process to uncover the truth.

South Carolina Law and Federal Trucking Regulations

While federal FMCSA rules set a national standard for truck safety, the legal aftermath of an accident is governed by state law. For victims in the Lowcountry, understanding South Carolina truck accident laws is essential for protecting their rights. These laws determine who can file a claim and what compensation they may be entitled to receive.

One of the most important local rules is South Carolina’s modified comparative fault standard. In simple terms, this means you can recover damages as long as you are found to be 50% or less at fault for the accident. If you are, your compensation will be reduced by your percentage of fault. This rule makes it critical to have a strong case proving the trucking company’s negligence.

Under state law, victims can seek two primary types of compensation:

  1. Economic Damages: These are tangible, calculable losses, including medical bills, rehabilitation costs, and lost income from being unable to work.
  2. Non-Economic Damages: These compensate for intangible losses that do not have a specific price tag, such as pain and suffering, emotional distress, and loss of quality of life.

Understanding how these laws apply to your situation is crucial, and our team at Roden Law is experienced in navigating both federal and state regulations for our clients.

Steps to Take After a Charleston Truck Accident

In the chaotic moments after a truck crash, it can be difficult to know what to do. Taking the right steps can protect your health and your legal rights.

  1. Ensure Safety and Report the Crash: Your first priority is safety. If you can, move your vehicle out of traffic. Call 911 immediately to report the accident and request medical assistance.
  2. Document Everything: Use your phone to take pictures of the accident scene, the positions of the vehicles, property damage, and any visible defects on the truck, like worn tires or broken parts.
  3. Seek a Full Medical Evaluation: Even if you feel fine, see a doctor. Adrenaline can mask serious injuries like concussions or internal bleeding that may not show symptoms for hours or days.
  4. Do Not Speak to Insurers: The trucking company’s insurance adjuster may contact you quickly. Avoid giving a recorded statement or signing any documents until you have spoken with an attorney.

Most importantly, consult with a legal professional. A Charleston truck accident lawyer is equipped to handle the complexities of these cases. Knowing where to find help is essential. When you are ready to take the next step, contact us for a direct consultation.

posts.post_title: Protecting Your Rights After a Myrtle Beach Car Accident
posts.post_content:
Immediate Steps for Safety at the Accident Scene

In the moments after a collision, adrenaline floods your system. It can easily mask serious injuries, making a calm assessment difficult. Before you do anything else, check yourself and your passengers for injuries. If there is any doubt about anyone's condition, call 911 immediately. Your health is the absolute first priority.

Once you've addressed immediate medical needs, your focus should shift to securing the scene. This is especially critical in a place like Myrtle Beach, where the heavy traffic on Highway 17 or the tourist congestion along Ocean Boulevard can create secondary dangers. Turn on your hazard lights to alert other drivers. If it is safe to do so and the vehicles are operable, move them to the shoulder to prevent further collisions.

Under South Carolina law, you are required to remain at the scene of an accident. It’s natural to feel shaken or even angry, but it is vital to avoid confrontation with the other driver. Focus on staying calm and breathing. This composure is not just for your well being; it prepares you to handle the crucial next steps with a clear head.

Gathering Critical Information and Evidence

With the scene secured, your role shifts to that of an investigator. The information you collect in these minutes forms the bedrock of any future insurance claim or legal action. It’s easy to forget details later, so meticulous documentation now is essential. Begin by exchanging information with the other driver, but be mindful of your words. Never apologize or admit fault, as even a simple "I'm sorry" can be misinterpreted by insurance companies.

Your smartphone is your most powerful tool here. Go beyond just taking pictures of the vehicle damage. Capture wide shots of the entire scene to show the context of the crash. Photograph skid marks, road debris, and the final resting positions of the vehicles. Document any relevant traffic signals, stop signs, and the current weather or road conditions. This comprehensive visual record helps paint a clear picture of what to do after car accident sc to protect your rights. Collisions involving larger vehicles can present more complex evidence challenges; you can learn more about incidents with commercial trucks by reviewing resources from experienced truck accident lawyers.

Finally, look for independent eyewitnesses. A third party account can be invaluable. Politely ask anyone who saw the crash for their name and phone number. A simple, "Did you see what happened? Would you be willing to share your contact information in case it's needed?" is all it takes.

On-Scene Evidence Checklist
Evidence Type What to Capture Why It's Important
Other Driver's Information Name, address, phone, license number, insurance policy number Essential for filing a claim and for your lawyer to contact the at-fault party.
Vehicle Photographs Damage to all cars, license plates, position of vehicles Provides indisputable proof of the collision's impact and vehicle identification.
Scene Photographs Skid marks, debris, traffic signs, weather/road conditions Helps accident reconstruction experts establish how the crash occurred and who was at fault.
Eyewitness Information Full name and phone number of anyone who saw the crash Offers an unbiased, third-party account that can support your version of events.

Fulfilling Official Reporting Requirements

While you gather your own evidence, it is equally important to fulfill your legal obligations. In South Carolina, you must report car accident myrtle beach incidents to the police if there are any injuries, deaths, or apparent property damage of $1,000 or more. This is not an optional step. The responding officer will create an official police report, which often includes an FR-10 form verifying insurance information. This document becomes a critical piece of evidence for your claim.

When speaking with the officer, be factual and stick to what you know for certain. Avoid guessing about speeds or distances. Simply state the facts as you remember them. As noted by legal experts at FindLaw, calling the police to create an official record is one of the most critical follow-up steps, as this report is foundational for any subsequent proceedings.

It's also important to understand that reporting to the police is separate from your duty to your own insurance provider. Your policy is a contract that requires you to notify your insurer promptly after any accident, regardless of who was at fault. Failing to do so could jeopardize your coverage when you need it most.

Seeking and Documenting Medical Attention

After a crash, your health must be your top concern. The adrenaline that helped you at the scene can also hide serious conditions. Delayed-onset injuries like whiplash, concussions, or even internal bleeding may not present symptoms for hours or days. For this reason, you should seek a medical evaluation immediately, even if you feel fine. This visit creates a crucial baseline record that directly links any medical issues to the collision.

From that first visit onward, meticulous documentation is key to protecting your rights after a car accident injury in myrtle beach sc. Create a dedicated file for all medical paperwork and keep everything, including:

  • Official diagnoses and treatment plans
  • Prescription receipts and medication lists
  • Notes from physical therapy or specialist sessions
  • All medical bills and explanation of benefits statements

This file is more than just a collection of papers; it is the evidence that proves the extent of your injuries. Furthermore, it is essential that you follow your doctor's orders precisely. Insurance companies often argue that a patient who misses appointments or fails to follow a treatment plan must not be as injured as they claim. Diligent adherence to your care plan is vital for both your recovery and the strength of your legal claim. Documenting your injuries is the first step, but a Myrtle Beach personal injury lawyer can help you understand the full value of your medical records and future care needs.

Navigating Insurance Communications and Legal Counsel

Soon after the accident, you will likely receive a call from the other driver's insurance adjuster. Be prepared. Their job is to protect their company's bottom line, not to ensure you are fairly compensated. We strongly advise that you do not give a recorded statement to an opposing insurance adjuster without first speaking to an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions designed to elicit responses that can be used to minimize or deny your claim.

This is where a lawyer acts as a protective barrier, handling all communications and negotiations on your behalf. But when should you hire a myrtle beach car accident lawyer? Consider it essential in these scenarios:

  1. You or a passenger suffered significant injuries that require ongoing medical care.
  2. The other driver is disputing fault or changing their story.
  3. The insurance company has made a lowball offer that doesn't cover your expenses.
  4. The entire process feels overwhelming and you need an advocate on your side.

Many people hesitate due to cost concerns, but most personal injury lawyers work on a contingency fee basis. This means there is no fee unless you win your case. If you've been in a collision, the right team of car accident lawyers can handle the complexities while you focus on recovery. When you're ready to discuss your case, you can contact us for a free consultation.

Preserving Long-Term Evidence for Your Claim

The evidence you gathered at the scene was just the beginning. Building a strong claim requires ongoing, organized documentation. Create a single file, whether physical or digital, and place every single piece of paper related to the accident inside it. This includes the final police report, all medical bills as they arrive, vehicle repair estimates, and receipts for any out-of-pocket costs like prescriptions or a rental car.

You should also track any lost income. Keep copies of your pay stubs to show your regular earnings and ask your employer for a letter detailing the time you missed from work. Most importantly, start a "pain and suffering" journal. Each day, take a few moments to write down your pain levels, any sleep disruptions, challenges with daily tasks, and the emotional toll of the accident. This journal is a powerful tool for demonstrating the full human impact of the collision, which is vital under south carolina accident laws for recovering damages that go beyond simple medical bills. By diligently preserving evidence, you build a strong foundation for your claim. For more resources and comprehensive legal support, our firm is dedicated to helping accident victims.
